question: A cloud support agent attempts three different tool-based remediation steps to fix a customer's stuck deployment, and each attempt fails to resolve the issue. No further remediation options are available to the agent. What should happen next?
options: A) Escalate the case to a human agent, since the agent is unable to make further meaningful progress
B) Close the case as unresolvable, without any handoff to a human agent for further troubleshooting
C) Continue retrying the same remediation steps, since repeated attempts eventually resolve most stuck deployments
D) Inform the customer the issue is resolved, since the remediation steps were the correct actions to attempt
correct_answers: A) Escalate the case to a human agent, since the agent is unable to make further meaningful progress
explanations: Correct - inability to make meaningful progress after exhausting available remediation options is a clear escalation trigger.
Incorrect - closing the case without escalating abandons the customer instead of routing them to someone who can continue troubleshooting.
Incorrect - repeating the same failed steps without new options is unlikely to produce a different outcome and delays needed escalation.
Incorrect - telling the customer the issue is resolved when the deployment is still stuck is factually inaccurate.
